scope: Refresh portion of rules database from immigration.gov.np and indembkathmandu.gov.in for two Indian nationals on a 14-day Nepal road trip departing 2026-05-09.

facts.title: Indian nationals do not require a visa for tourism in Nepal
facts.detail: Nepal Immigration's 'Information for Indian Nationals' page lists only identity-document requirements (no visa is referenced). The Visa Exemption page lists countries with diplomatic/official-passport exemptions and does not include India because Indian ordinary-passport holders enter under the bilateral 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship and never required a visa in the first place.
facts.value: visa-free for tourism (no Nepal visa required for Indian citizens)

facts.title: Acceptable identity documents for Indian citizens by AIR (per Nepal Immigration)
facts.detail: Nepal Immigration page lists four documents for air travel between India and Nepal: (i) valid national passport, (ii) Election ID card issued by ECI, (iii) Emergency Certificate issued by Embassy of India, Kathmandu, (iv) Identity Certificate issued by Embassy of India, Kathmandu. Aadhaar (UID) is explicitly NOT acceptable. Embassy-issued Certificate of Registration is NOT acceptable. Persons over 65 or under 15 are exempt from these four but must carry photo ID showing age. Children 15-18 may travel on a school-principal-issued identity certificate. Emergency/Identity Certificates are valid only for single journey back to India.
facts.notes: Page is titled 'Identity documents required for Indian citizen going to/coming from Nepal by Air'. It does not state the rules for land/road entry. PAN card is not listed as acceptable on either site.

facts.title: Acceptable identity documents for Indian citizens by AIR (per Indian Embassy Kathmandu)
facts.detail: Embassy lists ONLY two valid documents for Indian nationals travelling by air between India and Nepal: (1) valid Indian passport, OR (2) original Indian Voter ID card with photograph (issued by Election Commission of India). Downloaded/online-print Voter ID cards are NOT acceptable. Aadhaar, PAN card, Driving Licence, Indian Embassy Registration are NOT accepted.
value: Original ECI Voter ID card with photograph
facts.notes: Embassy lists only 2 documents (passport or original Voter ID). Nepal Immigration also accepts Embassy-issued Emergency Cert and Identity Cert. Both sites are unambiguous that Aadhaar and PAN are NOT acceptable. Both pages explicitly cover AIR travel; rules for land/road entry not stated on either page.

facts.title: Indian-registered vehicles allowed maximum 30 days/calendar year in Nepal
facts.detail: Indian-registered vehicles (motorcycles, cars, vans, jeeps, trucks, etc.) are temporarily importable into Nepal on payment of customs duty. Total stay is capped at 30 days per calendar year, even with payment. A Pass/Challan must be obtained at the Nepalese border check post; charges are NRs. 100-500 per day depending on vehicle type. A Day Pass requires same-day return. Pass extension can be done at the issuing border post or Nepal Customs office at TIA Cargo Complex (Kathmandu). Vehicles caught without a valid Pass are treated as smuggled and may be seized/auctioned.

extensionLocations: border check post that issued the Pass
Nepal Customs at TIA Cargo Complex, Kathmandu

facts.notes: Highly relevant for the 14-day road trip. Charges quoted in NRs and 30-day annual cap implies the trip must end within the cap; if user has used Indian-vehicle days earlier in calendar 2026, they should subtract from 30. Embassy page redirects users to www.customs.gov.np for current Customs Tariff.
